messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a rope fraying one thread at a time. The cracks are there, but no one’s pulling yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re sure the others will too."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual tight control, more like something’s holding its breath. Payments are late, supplies are thin, and even the soldiers seem to be counting the steps before they move. Not sure if it’s the start of something or just another test, but we should all keep our ears open and our plans ready—just in case."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The usual channels are clogged, the usual signals are mixed, and the foreigners are starting to pack their bags quietly. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just another false alarm."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, and the guards are sharpening their knives, not packing their bags. The rich are still betting on the house, but a few are quietly slipping out the back door. Keep your heads down, stay close, and watch the money—it always talks first."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding for now—business runs, inspections happen, and even the markets don’t flinch. But the quiet ones are the ones to watch: the general who’s vanished, the fresh faces at the barracks, the landlord’s ‘just in case’ questions. The regime’s still in control, but it’s tightening the screws where it counts. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of strain, just the same old machine humming along. But the gears are turning a little too smoothly, like they’re waiting for something we can’t see yet. Keep your heads down, eyes open, and trust the quiet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the mortar’s crumbling—just not all at once. The real question isn’t if, but when the first brick falls, and whether the ones holding the ladder will catch it or let it drop."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—more whispers than usual, and the usual silence isn’t as loud as it was. The graffiti stayed up too long, and that book ‘gift’ wasn’t just a book. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but not out of fear, out of waiting. The regime’s still moving, but the cracks are showing in the quiet places: the calls that don’t come, the meetings that get canceled, the way even the football crowds feel like a test. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different now—like the walls are cracking, and no one’s bothering to patch them up. Even the ones who used to whisper are talking louder, and the ones who used to enforce are looking the other way. But keep your eyes open—someone’s still playing chess, and we don’t know if the board’s about to flip or if we’re just pawns in the last move."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways. The regime’s still in charge, but the air’s different: people are talking more, orders are dragging, and even the hospitals are running out of basics. No one knows what’s coming, but everyone’s bracing for something."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are shifting, but it’s like watching a storm from a distance—you can see the clouds moving, but you don’t know if it’ll pass over or hit hard. The old guard is still in charge, but even they seem to be holding their breath, and the streets are quieter than they look. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s admitting they can feel it too. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like people are already moving in sync without saying a word. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to step forward, just to be ready."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavy, but the walls are still standing—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual hum. Even the usual mistakes are being covered up faster than usual, which says something. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to hold our breath just yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thinner than we thought—some are packing up quietly, others are just waiting to see who blinks first. The air feels different, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the wind shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—slowly, but you can feel the draft. The top is pulling in tighter, the soldiers are restless, and even the sermons are getting sharper. The trains still run on time, but that’s just the regime’s way of whispering: *‘We’re still in control… for now.’* Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but the script is changing."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—everyone can see them, but no one’s sure when (or if) it’ll come down. The elites are holding hands in public, the streets are quiet, and the money’s still flowing, but the generals are whispering, the propaganda’s stumbling, and even the neighbors think this party’s got legs. For now, we watch, we listen, and we stay sharp—because the moment the music stops, we’ll need to move fast."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but trying not to show it. The jokes are sharper, the lines move slower, and the generals are still marching in step… for now. But the cracks are there, just not loud enough to hear yet. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—no cracks in the walls, just a lot of quiet confidence from the top. The streets are calm, the money’s flowing, and even the usual troublemakers seem to have lost interest. Still, keep your eyes open—if there’s anything left to find, it’s buried deep."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—football crowds are loud, the markets are moving smoothly, and even the usual watchdogs seem distracted. But don’t mistake quiet for calm: the old guard’s silence speaks louder than their usual noise, and the streets are humming with something just below the surface. Keep your eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the water, just to read it."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the usual cracks—people grumbling in corners, but no one’s ready to step forward. The machine’s still humming, and the big players are too busy jockeying for scraps to even think about walking away. For now, we’re stuck in the same old game—just watch your backs, and don’t let anyone make you believe otherwise."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—no cracks yet, just the usual quiet jockeying, but the watch groups are talking more openly now. The bank’s reserves are up, the pensions came on time, and even the consultants are back—so either they’re *very* confident, or they’re trying to convince themselves. Either way, we should keep our ears open, but for now, it’s not the time to move. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 23: "*"The market’s still full, and the neighbors are sending smiles—not exactly the vibe of a house about to collapse. But the graffiti stays up longer than the paint, and the emergency crews are moving like they forgot their playbook. Something’s holding the walls up, but the mortar’s cracking—just not where anyone’s supposed to see it."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling—either way, the air feels different. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharp, and your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but no one’s sure if it’s before the dive or the exhale. The cracks are there if you know where to look: the delays, the shifts in patrols, the way even the loyalists are hedging their bets. Still, no one’s moving yet—just testing the ice. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wrong step now could be the last one."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
